I've worked with 4 different systems, and none of the modern ones have any sort of ability to delete footage. They're super serious about that. But if you're the sysadmin, fuck it, you can just browse to the directory and delete it straight out of the file system. But that's why logging exists, so good luck getting away with that.

There are however a bunch of non-nefarious ways footage can go missing.

  • If the camera is physically damaged during the incident (car crash, gun fight, whatever), there's a solid chance you're not getting footage off. Had that happen a couple times, thankfully not on anything terribly important.

  • If the officer's body cam was malfunctioning for whatever reason (It's a basically a small shitty computer with a webcam stuck to it, they break easy) before the incident, and he didn't get the tech to fix it yet, you're not going to get footage because it was never recorded in the first place.

  • If the footage was never properly tagged, and got purged by the system's retention policy. Depending on the exact system in question, it can be super easy to tag something improperly.

  • If officer numb nuts (I kid, I love these guys), hasn't checked his email in the last month and hasn't seen all my emails telling him to get his down here so I can update his wifi settings, the camera's never going to offload footage, and it's missing until I can track his ass down. Seriously, it's like trying to herd cats sometimes.

  • If the docking station has gone tits up in just the right special way, it'll grab the footage off of the body cam, erase it from the body cam like it's supposed to, but then never upload the footage to the server. That really fucked with my head the first time.
